deltas.description: Totalized-gradient algebraic interface is broader than source classical derivative assumptions.
deltas.evidence: The two new declarations intentionally omit C1/C2. The gradient is Lean totalized fderiv passed through the Riesz map. It is not a freely supplied vector field, but one must not identify it with an existing classical derivative at arbitrary points. Lessons explicitly state this and the global model premise. Source smooth functions are a specialization; this is not source-equivalent regularity.

deltas.description: The printed step condition omits the necessary nonnegative lower bound.
deltas.evidence: f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1 satisfies h<=1/beta. T(1)=2; f(2)-f(1)=3/2 but -(h/2)|f prime(1)|^2=1/2, so descent fails. More generally h<0 gives discrepancy h(h-1)/2>0.

repairs.proposed_change: Add h>=0 to the printed h<=1/beta restriction in Lemma3.1. Retain the original pinned source separately and preserve the local algebraic generalization.
repairs.reconstructed_statement: Let f:R^d->R be C2 and beta-smooth with beta>0. For every step 0<=h<=1/beta and every x, define T(x)=x-h grad f(x). Then f(T(x))-f(x)<=-(h/2)||grad f(x)||^2.
repairs.justification: f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1 satisfies h<=1/beta. T(1)=2; f(2)-f(1)=3/2 but -(h/2)|f prime(1)|^2=1/2, so descent fails. More generally h<0 gives discrepancy h(h-1)/2>0.
repairs.minimality_evidence: Only the lower bound h>=0 is added to the source step domain; h=0 remains valid. Source positive modulus/regularity premises are retained. No convexity or strong convexity assumption is added. Omitting the new lower bound admits the explicit quadratic counterexample.
repairs.reference_or_counterexample: Primary source https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3, Lemma3.1. Exact counterexample: f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1 satisfies h<=1/beta. T(1)=2; f(2)-f(1)=3/2 but -(h/2)|f prime(1)|^2=1/2, so descent fails. More generally h<0 gives discrepancy h(h-1)/2>0.

review_evidence: Accepted scoped source support for Lemma3.1 with explicit h>=0 and separately disclosed totalized-gradient, signed-modulus, Hilbert-space generalization. The literal negative-step source assertion and any automatic source repair acceptance are excluded. Entire current Basic module and bound lesson/provenance reviewed. Insert T(x)=x-hg into the upper model. Inner product and norm identities give -h||g||^2+(beta/2)h^2||g||^2. From beta h<=1 times h||g||^2>=0 obtain exactly -(h/2)||g||^2. This does not require beta>=0 or a differentiability premise once that global model is assumed. The two new declarations intentionally omit C1/C2.
